title: Enabling Low-Overhead HT-HPC Workflows at Extreme Scale using GNU Parallel
problem: Large-scale high-throughput HPC workflows require efficient process-level parallelization with minimal overhead across diverse workload types. GNU Parallel's effectiveness and overhead characteristics at extreme scales on modern supercomputers need empirical validation.
motivation: Efficient workflow management at extreme scales is essential for maximizing scientific productivity and resource utilization on leadership-class supercomputers.
method: GNU Parallel allows many computing tasks to run at the same time across multiple computers in a supercomputer by quickly dispatching each task to available machines. The tool was tested on two leading-edge supercomputers—OLCF's Frontier and NERSC's Perlmutter—with diverse workloads including GPU computing, containerized software, and fast storage operations (NVMe). GNU Parallel can work independently to manage entire computational workflows or integrate with other workflow systems to handle the final parallelization stage, all while using minimal computing resources for coordination.
key_novelty: GNU Parallel effectively manages high-throughput computing workloads (many independent computing tasks) at extreme scales on leadership supercomputers without significant overhead.
contributions: Empirical evaluation of GNU Parallel performance on Frontier and Perlmutter supercomputers
Characterization of rapid process dispatching and low overhead maintenance at extreme scale
